title: He Lost His Central Contract. He Went Home to Jharkhand. On Saturday, He Walks Back Into India's ODI Squad.
excerpt: Ishan Kishan returns to India's ODI setup for the first time since the 2023 World Cup — nearly three years and a state title later
body:
The last time Ishan Kishan played an ODI for India, the World Cup was on home soil and the team seemed invincible. It was October 2023, India were in the middle of a perfect group-stage run, and Kishan — a compact, fearless left-hander with a double century against Bangladesh already on his record — looked like a fixture in the setup for years to come.

Then, quietly and somewhat mysteriously, he disappeared.

He requested a personal break. The BCCI granted it. Weeks turned into months. He missed domestic cricket. He lost his central contract — one of the most visible markers of status in Indian cricket. Head coach Rahul Dravid, diplomatic as ever, left the door open but made his position clear: "Whenever he's ready, he needs to play some cricket and come back, and the choice is his."

For a while, Kishan did not make that choice. He was, by all available accounts, working through something private. The cricketing world — which is notably bad at giving young men space — speculated freely. Was he burned out? Disillusioned? Had something happened in the dressing room?

Nobody outside Kishan's inner circle knows the full story. What is known is what happened next.

## The Jharkhand Road

In late 2024, Kishan returned to domestic cricket. Not with a whisper — with a statement. He led Jharkhand to their maiden **Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy** title, the state's first national title in men's cricket. His batting was clinical. More importantly, his body language had changed. He looked like someone who had found the thing that had gone missing.

The selectors noticed. He was recalled for T20 Internationals ahead of the 2026 T20 World Cup, where he impressed with consistent performances. He followed it with a commanding IPL 2026 season for Sunrisers Hyderabad — **602 runs in 15 matches** — consistently batting at the pace and with the assurance that had made him such an exciting prospect in the first place.

Former teammate Ambati Rayudu credited Kishan's resurgence to the move from Mumbai Indians to Hyderabad, saying it gave him the space to grow without the weight of Mumbai's legacy on his shoulders.

## The Number Three Question

On Saturday, when India take the field in Dharamsala for the first ODI of a historic bilateral series against Afghanistan, Kishan is expected to bat at number three. It is the spot vacated by Virat Kohli, who has been ruled out with a rare hamstring injury sustained in the IPL final.

Former India opener Aakash Chopra has publicly backed Kishan for the role, calling him "God's favourite child" and pointing to his extraordinary knack for seizing opportunities whenever they arise.

"He is scoring runs at the No. 3 spot, and the southpaw is in good form," Chopra said. "Whenever the doors open, Kishan walks in. He is standing when the door is opened, and when he walks in, the runs flow from his bat."

The numbers support the enthusiasm. Kishan has 933 runs in 27 ODIs at an average of 42.40, with a strike rate of 102.19. His best score remains the historic 210 he made against Bangladesh in December 2022 — at the time, the fastest double century in ODI history by an Indian.

Yashasvi Jaiswal, who was called in as Kohli's squad replacement, is the other contender for the spot. But Kishan's experience in the middle order and his current form give him a strong case.

## What It Means

There is something in Kishan's story that resonates beyond cricket. The narrative of the comeback — of losing status, going home, rebuilding in obscurity, and returning stronger — is a template that many in the Indian diaspora recognize. It is the story of the professional who lost a visa and started over. The entrepreneur whose first venture failed. The student who took a gap year and came back to finish what they started.

India's first-ever bilateral ODI series against Afghanistan begins at 1:30 PM IST on Saturday, June 13, at the HPCA Stadium in Dharamsala. The remaining matches are in Lucknow (June 17) and Chennai (June 20). All three will be broadcast on Star Sports and streamed on JioHotstar.
